scenes.title: The Happy Darling Household
scenes.summary: Warm introduction to the Darling family at No.14: Wendy learning she must grow up, her romantic mother and practical father, keeping the children despite expenses, and their dog-nurse Nana presiding over a simple happy household.

scenes.title: Tidying Children's Minds
scenes.summary: Mrs. Darling tidies her sleeping children's minds each night like drawers, folding away naughtiness and airing prettier thoughts for morning.

scenes.title: Mapping Neverland
scenes.summary: A child's mind is mapped as a shifting Neverland island, snug and compact and different for John, Michael and Wendy, where Mrs. Darling keeps finding the perplexing, cocky-looking name Peter.

muse_override.reason: Whimsical map of children's minds blends wonder, playful mystery and nostalgic warmth.

scenes.title: Who Is Peter Pan
scenes.summary: The perplexing word Peter appears scrawled through the children's minds; Wendy admits he is rather cocky, Mrs. Darling recalls the fairy Peter Pan, and Mr. Darling dismisses it as Nana's nonsense.

scenes.title: Leaves by the Window
scenes.summary: Wendy casually reveals Peter visits by the window at night, leaving strange leaves; Mrs. Darling searches floor, chimney and sheer drop below, and uneasily concludes Wendy must have been dreaming.

scenes.title: Quiet Night in the Nursery
scenes.summary: On Nana's evening off, Mrs. Darling bathes the children, puts them safely to bed, and settles to sew by the fire until her head nods and she falls asleep in the dim nursery.

scenes.title: Peter Breaks Through
scenes.summary: Mrs. Darling dreams the Neverland has come too near and a strange boy breaks through; the window blows open and Peter Pan drops in with a darting fairy light as she wakes with a cry.

muse_override.reason: Dreamlike intrusion and darting fairy light create mysterious wonder with a sudden startled awakening.

scenes.title: Nana's Spring and the Snapped-Off Shadow
scenes.summary: Nana returns and springs at the boy, who leaps through the nursery window; Mrs. Darling fears him killed and finds only Nana holding his detached shadow, snapped off by the closing window.

scenes.title: The Shadow Rolled Away in a Drawer
scenes.summary: Mrs. Darling finds the shadow ordinary, rejects Nana's plan to hang it at the window like washing, spares the busy Mr. Darling, and rolls it away in a drawer.

muse_override.reason: Quiet domestic handling of an uncanny shadow blends calm routine with mystery and wistful foreboding.

scenes.title: Remorse Over That Fatal Friday
scenes.summary: Sitting in the empty nursery, the Darlings and Nana guiltily recall the fatal Friday of the dinner invitation, each blaming their own party-love, humour, medicine trick, and touchiness for what followed.

scenes.title: A Tender Evening Before Bed
scenes.summary: The memory returns to a tender, ordinary evening: Michael resisting his bath, Mrs. Darling in her white evening-gown, and the children play-acting Wendy's birth and begging to be born again.

muse_override.reason: Warm domestic bedtime play full of love, shadowed by nostalgic sorrow of the empty-nursery recollection.

scenes.title: The Tornado Over the Tie
scenes.summary: Mr. Darling recalls rushing into the nursery like a tornado, furious because his tie will not tie and threatening that without it there will be no dinner, no office, and ruin.

muse_override.reason: Comic paternal bluster turns a tie struggle into playful domestic battle.

scenes.title: Cool Hands and the Last Romp
scenes.summary: Mrs. Darling calmly ties the tie with her cool hands while the children watch, Mr. Darling forgets his rage and dances round the room with Michael, a wild romp the parents now mourn as their last.

scenes.title: Hairs on the Trousers and the Shadow Shown
scenes.summary: The romp ends when Mr. Darling collides with Nana and fumes about dog hairs on his braided trousers, then turns thoughtful as Mrs. Darling finally shows him the boy's shadow.

scenes.title: The Brave Medicine Boast
scenes.summary: Nana brings Michael's medicine, which Michael refuses. Mr. Darling scolds him for lack of firmness and boasts that he took medicine bravely as a child and takes far nastier stuff himself, claiming he would prove it if he had not lost the bottle, which he has secretly hidden atop the wardrobe after Liza restored it.

muse_override.reason: Comedic paternal boasting and cozy nursery antics make it warmly playful.

scenes.title: Father First Standoff
scenes.summary: Wendy eagerly fetches her father's hidden medicine, to his dismay. Mr. Darling tries to delay by insisting Michael drink first, while Michael insists on father first. Cornered, Mr. Darling protests the dose is larger and unfair as John and Wendy press him to keep his brave example.

muse_override.reason: Comedic family standoff with tense bickering over unfair medicine dose.

scenes.title: A Cruel Joke on Nana
scenes.summary: Father and son call each other cowardly custard and count to take medicine together, but Mr. Darling cheats. To save face he pours his dose into Nana's milk bowl, enduring reproachful stares and Nana's wounded, tearful look.

scenes.title: Nana Banished to the Yard
scenes.summary: Ashamed yet craving mastery, Mr. Darling rages against being uncoddled, overrules tears and warnings about the boy, drags protesting Nana from her kennel, and chains her in the back-yard.

scenes.title: Danger in Nana's Bark
scenes.summary: Mrs. Darling puts the silent children to bed amid Nana's barking. Wendy insists it is not unhappiness but danger-smelling, filling Mrs. Darling with nameless fear as she checks the fastened window.

scenes.title: Night-Lights and Now, Peter!
scenes.summary: Reassuring Michael that lit night-lights guard them, Mrs. Darling sings over the beds and leaves for No. 27 with her husband through snow while watching stars gather, until the smallest star screams for Peter.

muse_override.reason: Tender night-light lullaby turns ominous as watchful stars conspire to summon Peter.

scenes.title: Night Lights Out and Peter Arrives
scenes.summary: After the Darlings leave, the three night-lights yawn and go out. Tinker Bell's flashing fairy light darts through the nursery searching drawers, wardrobe, and pockets for Peter's shadow. Peter drops in through the window and calls softly for Tink, who answers in fairy tinkle from inside a jug.

muse_override.reason: Magical night arrival of glowing fairy and Peter evokes wonder and mystery amid sleeping calm.

scenes.title: Shadow Found and Soap Fails
scenes.summary: Tink tells Peter his shadow is in the chest of drawers, and he recovers it while scattering the drawers and shutting Tink inside. When the shadow will not join like drops of water and soap fails to stick it on, Peter sits on the floor and cries.

scenes.title: Wendy Wakes to Meet Peter
scenes.summary: Wendy wakes and politely meets the crying boy. They exchange names, his strange Neverland address, and his proud claim to have no mother, which strikes Wendy as tragic.

muse_override.reason: Gentle midnight meeting full of polite wonder and playful mystery with a touch of tender sadness.

scenes.title: Sewing on the Shadow
scenes.summary: Wendy pities the draggled shadow and sews it to Peter's foot with her housewife. Peter endures without crying, then forgets her help and crows over his own cleverness.

scenes.title: Conceit and Thimble Kisses
scenes.summary: Wendy is stung by Peter's conceit and withdraws under the blankets until he flatters her. They exchange innocent tokens of a thimble for a kiss and an acorn button for a kiss.

scenes.title: Never Grow Up and Fairy Lore
scenes.summary: Wendy asks Peter's age. He tells of running away at birth to avoid growing up, living among fairies, and explains that fairies are born from a baby's first laugh and die when children disbelieve.

scenes.title: Tinker Bell Released in a Fury
scenes.summary: Remembering Tinker Bell, Peter finds he shut her in the drawer. Wendy glimpses her on the cuckoo clock, but jealous Tink insults Wendy and retreats to the bathroom as a common pot-mending fairy.

muse_override.reason: Merry laughter and furious fairy antics blend childlike wonder with playful joy.

scenes.title: The Lost Boys and Lonely Captain
scenes.summary: In the armchair Peter describes the lost boys of Neverland and their lonely lack of female companionship. He kicks sleeping John from bed to prove he is not captain in Wendy's house.

muse_override.reason: Playful nursery banter with wistful Neverland lore calls for warm joyful wonder.

scenes.title: Jealous Fairy and Hungry for Stories
scenes.summary: A second kiss-thimble provokes Tink to pull Wendy's hair. Peter admits he came to hear stories, and Wendy tempts him by revealing the end of Cinderella and her store of stories.

muse_override.reason: Playful thimble-kiss comedy with Tink's jealous sting and Peter's story-hunger favors bright joy.

scenes.title: Come Away to Neverland
scenes.summary: Peter lures Wendy to the window with promises of flying, stars, mermaids, respect, and tucking and darning for the boys. Won over, Wendy agrees if John and Michael may learn to fly and wakes them.

muse_override.reason: Childlike wonder at flying, stars and mermaids drives adventure and awe.

scenes.title: Hiding and Nana's Alarm
scenes.summary: The children hide behind curtains as Liza drags protesting Nana in and dismisses her fears. Nana breaks her chain to alarm the dining room, sending Mr. and Mrs. Darling rushing home while Peter uses ten precious minutes.

scenes.title: Fairy Dust and First Flight
scenes.summary: Peter demonstrates flight, then reveals the secret of fairy dust and blows it on them. The nursery fills with joyous, clumsy soaring as John, Michael, and Wendy bob against the ceiling.

muse_override.reason: Joyful first flight brims with playful delight and childlike wonder.

scenes.title: Too Late - The Birds Are Flown
scenes.summary: Lured by pirates and mermaids, the children decide to go out. Below, the Darlings see four circling shadows on the curtain, but warned by the stars, Peter leads the three children out the window just before the parents rush in too late.

scenes.title: Straight On Till Morning
scenes.summary: Peter's vague directions to the Neverland launch the flight, as the children revel in the sheer delight of flying, circling spires and racing.

scenes.title: The Perils of Flying
scenes.summary: The long journey over seas and night brings cold, hunger, and exhaustion. Peter feeds them by robbing birds and laughs as they fall asleep and drop, while Wendy realizes they depend on him completely and do not know how to stop.

scenes.title: A Forgetful Guide
scenes.summary: Peter darts ahead on private adventures with stars and mermaids, returning forgetful. Wendy fears he will forget them too, and he begs her to remind him who she is.

scenes.title: First Sight of Neverland
scenes.summary: Guided by golden arrows of sunlight, the island appears. The children joyfully recognize the lagoon, turtles, flamingo, cave, wolves, boat, and redskin camp as old friends.

muse_override.reason: Wondrous island reveal blends awe, adventure, and joyful homecoming.

scenes.title: Fear Falls
scenes.summary: Darkness falls and the make-believe island turns real and threatening. The children huddle to Peter as the air itself resists landing, while he beats it back and sends Tink ahead.

scenes.title: Tea First
scenes.summary: Hovering over the fearsome island, Peter casually offers adventure or tea, proposing to wake and kill a sleeping pirate below. John chooses tea after hearing how many pirates there are.

scenes.title: The Name of Hook
scenes.summary: Peter names the captain as Jas. Hook, sending terror through John and Michael. He sternly reveals he cut off Hook's right hand, to the boys' awe.

scenes.title: Leave Him to Me
scenes.summary: Peter describes Hook's iron hook claw and extracts a solemn promise from John that if they meet Hook in open fight, Hook must be left to Peter alone.

scenes.title: A Halo That Betrays Them
scenes.summary: Tink circles the children in a halo of fairy light until Peter warns that the pirates have sighted it and readied Long Tom. The children beg him to send her away or dim her light, but fairies cannot put out their light except in sleep.

scenes.title: The Light in the Hat
scenes.summary: Unable to make Tink sleep, Peter hides her light in John's hat. John carries it, then passes it to Wendy, leaving Tink resentful at being under an obligation to her rival.

scenes.title: Long Tom Fires
scenes.summary: Stillness breaks with drinking beasts and sharpening knives, then the tremendous crash of Long Tom. The blast scatters them into darkness, Peter blown out to sea and Wendy upward alone.

scenes.title: Tink's Betrayal
scenes.summary: Alone with only mocking echoes answering her calls, bewildered Wendy follows Tink, who, all jealousy in her tiny frame, sweetly lures her toward destruction.

scenes.title: The Island Wakes
scenes.summary: The island wakes with Peter's return. Its four forces circle each other endlessly at the same pace, never meeting, the whole island seething with life.

scenes.title: Tootles Leads the File
scenes.summary: The six lost boys steal by in single file in bearskins, and Tootles passes first, the humblest and most unlucky of them, whom the mischievous Tinker Bell marks as her tool.

scenes.title: Nibs, Slightly, Curly and the Twins
scenes.summary: Tootles passes biting his knuckles, followed by Nibs, Slightly, Curly, and last the vague, inseparable Twins.

scenes.title: Hook and His Pirates
scenes.summary: The pirates follow singing their dreadful song. Hook is revealed in all his elegant menace, iron claw, melancholy eyes and cruelty, demonstrated when he casually kills Skylights.

scenes.title: Redskins, Beasts and Crocodile
scenes.summary: Redskins glide noiselessly past, led by Great Big Little Panther and Tiger Lily, followed by hungry beasts and lastly the gigantic crocodile, all watching ahead but not behind.

scenes.title: Boys Long for Peter
scenes.summary: The boys drop by their underground home, wishing for Peter's return. In his absence they dare to talk sentimentally of mothers and Cinderella.

scenes.title: Vanishing Underground
scenes.summary: Hearing the pirate song, the boys vanish instantly. All but Nibs slip down the seven hollow trees into their hidden underground home Hook has long sought.

scenes.title: Hook Holds His Fire
scenes.summary: Starkey spots Nibs but Hook stops the shot for fear of bringing Tiger Lily's redskins. Hook sends the crew searching and remains alone with Smee, sighing to confide his story.

scenes.title: Hook's Dread
scenes.summary: Hook confesses his obsession: Peter cut off his arm and fed it to a crocodile that now follows him everywhere, betrayed only by the ticking clock it swallowed.

scenes.title: The Poison Cake Plot
scenes.summary: Sitting on a hot mushroom, Hook discovers the boys' chimney. Overhearing them, he hatches his wickedest plan: a poisoned green-sugar cake left at Mermaids' Lagoon for motherless boys.

scenes.title: Tick Tick Terror
scenes.summary: Triumph turns to terror as tick-tick announces the crocodile. Shuddering, Hook flees with Smee close behind while the beast oozes on after him.

scenes.title: Wolves Defied
scenes.summary: Nibs bursts in pursued by wolves. Remembering Peter, the boys bend and look through their legs, and the terrible attitude sends the pack fleeing.

scenes.title: Shoot the Wendy
scenes.summary: Nibs reports a weary white bird moaning 'Poor Wendy.' As Wendy flies overhead tormented by Tink, the fairy lies that Peter wants the Wendy shot, and obedient Tootles fires his bow.

scenes.title: The Slain Lady
scenes.summary: Tootles boasts of shooting Wendy, then horror falls as the boys realize she is not a bird but a lady Peter was bringing to mother them. Tootles is stricken with guilt and fears Peter's return.

muse_override.reason: Mourning guilt over killing Wendy dominates, with fearful suspense as Peter's crow approaches.

scenes.title: Peter's Return and Wrath
scenes.summary: Peter crows his return and proudly announces a mother, only to be met with silence. Shown Wendy's body, he demands whose arrow struck her and raises it to punish Tootles, who bares his breast, but Peter's hand stays.

scenes.title: She Lives
scenes.summary: Wendy stirs and is found alive, saved by Peter's kiss-button stopping the arrow. Joy turns stern as Peter learns Tink's treachery and banishes her for a week despite her pleading.

scenes.title: A House Round Her
scenes.summary: Faced with Wendy's delicate state, the boys debate carrying her indoors until Peter forbids touching her and orders them to build a little house around her.

muse_override.reason: Urgent tenderness turning into joyful childlike building adventure around fragile Wendy.

scenes.title: Recruits for Building
scenes.summary: John and Michael stumble in exhausted from flying and are startled to find the camp building. Peter presses them into service as Wendy's servants to fetch chairs and build the house.

muse_override.reason: Busy cheerful house-building for Wendy is playful adventure with wonder.

scenes.title: The Make-Believe Doctor
scenes.summary: Peter orders a doctor in full make-believe earnest. Slightly dons John's hat, solemnly examines the unseen lady with a glass thing, pronounces her cured, and prescribes beef tea.

muse_override.reason: Playful make-believe curing is joyful and adventurous with brief anxious suspense.

scenes.title: Building the Little House
scenes.summary: Axes ring as the boys gather materials and sing with the sleeping Wendy to shape her dream house of red walls, moss roof, roses and windows, finishing it with a shoe knocker and John's hat for a smoking chimney.

scenes.title: A Knock At The Little House
scenes.summary: Peter warns the boys to look their best and knocks ceremoniously while Tink sneers from a branch. Wendy opens the door to delighted hats-off welcome, admires the lovely house built for her, and hears the kneeling boys beg her to be their mother, while she hesitates as only a little girl without experience.

scenes.title: Wendy Takes Her Children
scenes.summary: Peter assures Wendy that a nice motherly person is enough, and she joyfully accepts, bustling the damp-footed children inside for Cinderella before bed. That first joyous evening ends with the boys tucked in the home under the trees and Wendy safe in the cosy lamplit house while Peter stands guard with drawn sword against distant pirates and prowling wolves, then dozes as fairies tweak his nose passing home.

muse_override.reason: Cozy motherly safety dominates with joyful warmth and only distant pirate danger.

scenes.title: Measured for Hollow Trees
scenes.summary: Peter measures Wendy, John, and Michael for their hollow trees, explaining that unless the tree fits exactly you cannot go up and down gracefully.

scenes.title: The House Under the Ground
scenes.summary: After Wendy and Michael fit at once and John is altered, they learn to rise and sink gaily, and their underground home is described, from mushroom stools and the Never-tree table to the sardine bed, ending with Tinker Bell's exquisite private boudoir.

scenes.title: Wendy's Motherly Routine
scenes.summary: Wendy settles into endless motherly work, cooking make-believe meals at Peter's whim, sewing after bedtime, joking about spinsters, and reuniting joyfully with her pet wolf who follows her everywhere.

muse_override.reason: Cozy domestic mothering with playful make-believe warmth dominates the scene.

scenes.title: Forgetting Mother and Father
scenes.summary: A bittersweet shift as Wendy realizes John and Michael are forgetting their London parents. She gives them school-like examination papers about Mother and Father, which even John fails, while Peter refuses to compete and cannot write.

muse_override.reason: Wendy's quiet forgetting of home brings tender melancholic sadness.

scenes.title: The Game of Having No Adventures
scenes.summary: Peter, with Wendy's help, invents a new game of pretending not to have adventures, imitating ordinary life like sitting on stools, throwing balls, and walking for health, which fascinates him until he abruptly loses interest.

scenes.title: Tossing to Choose an Adventure
scenes.summary: The narrator explains how hard it is to know which of Peter's adventures are true, catalogs specimen island adventures at Slightly Gulch, the underground house, Tiger Lily, the poisoned cake, the Never bird, Tink's leaf plot, and the lions, then tosses to choose, and the lagoon wins.

scenes.title: Mermaids Snub Wendy and Play at Bubbles
scenes.summary: The narrator evokes the dreamlike lagoon and sunny swimming days, where the mermaids bask on Marooners' Rock, snub Wendy and the boys, chat only with Peter, and play their rainbow bubble games in great numbers after rain.

scenes.title: Midday Rest on Marooners' Rock
scenes.summary: Excluded from the bubble games, the children play alone while the watching mermaids secretly copy John's head-hit, then rest sun-glistening on Marooners' Rock after their make-believe midday meal as Wendy watches and stitches.

scenes.title: Shadows Over Marooners' Rock
scenes.summary: As Wendy stitches while the children doze, a cold shiver crosses the water, the sun dies, and tales of drowning on Marooners' Rock return as muffled oars approach and she refuses to wake them.

scenes.title: Pirates! Dive!
scenes.summary: Peter sniffs danger in his sleep, wakes the others with a cry of Pirates, and at his sharp order they dive, leaving the rock deserted in forbidding water.

scenes.title: Tiger Lily Brought to Die
scenes.summary: Smee and Starkey beach the dinghy with bound Tiger Lily, caught boarding the ship, to maroon her on the rock to drown as punishment and warning.

scenes.title: Peter's Voice Trick
scenes.summary: Hidden nearby, Peter imitates Hook's voice to order Tiger Lily set free, and the fooled pirates cut her bonds as she slips eel-like into the water while Wendy covers Peter's mouth to stop his crow.

scenes.title: The Real Hook Arrives
scenes.summary: The real Hook hails the boat and swims dripping to the lantern light, to Wendy's terror and Peter's top-heavy conceit as he whispers at his own wonder.

scenes.title: Hook's Melancholy Lesson
scenes.summary: Hook broods in melancholy over boys finding a mother, taught by the Never bird guarding its floating nest, while Smee asks what a mother is and Starkey fears she helps Peter.

muse_override.reason: Hook's mournful sighs over motherhood dominate while hidden listening sustains suspense.

scenes.title: The Oath to Seize Wendy
scenes.summary: Smee proposes kidnapping the boys' mother, Hook embraces the princely scheme to make the boys walk the plank and keep Wendy, and all swear by hand and hook.

scenes.title: The False Order
scenes.summary: Furious that Tiger Lily was freed on his supposed order, Hook denies giving it and challenges the spirit haunting the lagoon, which answers in his own voice claiming to be James Hook.

scenes.title: Only a Codfish
scenes.summary: The voice mocks Hook and dismisses him as only a codfish, breaking his proud spirit as his men draw back in contempt and he feels his ego slipping away.

scenes.title: The Guessing Game
scenes.summary: Guessing Hook intuits a game, Peter blithely answers yes and no through vegetable, mineral, animal, man, boy, and wonderful boy as Hook grows puzzled.

muse_override.reason: Tense verbal hide-and-seek builds suspense and mystery with playful defiance.

scenes.title: I Am Peter Pan
scenes.summary: Peter crows he cannot guess, reveals he is Peter Pan, and Hook instantly recovers, ordering Smee and Starkey into the water as Peter calls the boys to lam into the pirates.

scenes.title: Fair Play Betrayed
scenes.summary: A short sharp lagoon fight scatters the combatants until Peter and Hook meet face to face on the slippery rock, where Peter fairly offers a hand up and Hook unfairly bites him, then flees the crocodile as the boys sail home calling for Peter and Wendy.

scenes.title: Stranded on the Rising Rock
scenes.summary: In cold silence after the voices die, Peter drags fainting Wendy onto the shrinking rock, fights off a mermaid pulling her feet, and confesses Hook's wound leaves him unable to fly or swim to the island.

scenes.title: The Kite and the Big Adventure
scenes.summary: As the water rises they cover their eyes, then Michael's lost kite tail brushes Peter, who ties it round Wendy and pushes her to safety, left alone to hear the mermaids calling the moon and smile that to die will be an awfully big adventure.

scenes.title: Alone on the Rock
scenes.summary: Alone on the rock as the tide rises, Peter watches a speck fighting the tide and realizes it is the exhausted Never bird struggling to reach him with her nest to save him.

scenes.title: A Failure to Communicate
scenes.summary: Unable to understand each other's language, Peter and the bird try slow speech, grow irritated, trade insults, and both snap 'Shut up' at each other.

scenes.title: The Nest for a Hat
scenes.summary: The bird rams the nest against the rock and abandons her eggs to show her meaning; Peter understands, floats the eggs safely in Starkey's watertight hat, and sails ashore in the nest while they cheer each other.

scenes.title: Home Again Safe
scenes.summary: The hat-nest succeeds and changes how Never birds build forever, while Peter reaches the home under the ground to great rejoicing before Wendy sternly sends the late, adventure-swollen boys to bed.

scenes.title: The Great White Father
scenes.summary: After saving Tiger Lily, Peter has won the redskins' loyalty. They guard the underground home day and night and worship him as the Great White Father, which feeds his vanity while Wendy loyally defends his paternal role despite resenting being called a squaw.

scenes.title: The Noisy Make-Believe Tea
scenes.summary: On the fateful Night of Nights, the redskins stand watch above while the children have a rowdy make-believe tea below without Peter, who is out finding the crocodile to get the time. Wendy struggles to keep order as the boys chatter, grab, and tattle, and John challenges Peter's place as father.

scenes.title: Tootles Asks and the Last Cozy Fireside
scenes.summary: Humble Tootles wistfully asks to be father, baby, twin, or to do a trick, and is rebuffed. Complaining erupts again until Wendy sends them to clear away and sews while they play around her in a warm, familiar fireside tableau seen for the last time.

muse_override.reason: Cozy fireside playfulness tinged with farewell sadness as it is seen for the last time.

scenes.title: Father Comes Home
scenes.summary: Wendy recognizes Peter's step and the children drag him down from his tree for the last time. He brings nuts and the time, and in high good humour agrees the boys and Wendy may dance in their nighties for Saturday night.

scenes.title: Only Make-Believe
scenes.summary: Resting by the fire as pretend parents, Peter and Wendy share a tender domestic moment that turns uneasy when Peter admits fatherhood is only make-believe. Wendy presses him on his exact feelings, and is hurt when he says they are those of a devoted son.

scenes.title: Jealousies Over Peter
scenes.summary: Puzzled Peter mentions Tiger Lily wants to be something to him that is not his mother, provoking Wendy's sharp jealousy of both Tiger Lily and Tinker Bell. Tink eavesdrops and glories in being abandoned, and Wendy snaps, unaware of the danger coming that night.

muse_override.reason: Jealous bickering and puzzled innocence create comic rivalry tension, not true mystery.

scenes.title: The Last Glad Hour
scenes.summary: In ignorance of their fate, the children enjoy one last glad hour of singing, dancing, pillow-fighting, and stories in their nightgowns. They climb into bed for Wendy's beloved story that Peter hates, while Peter unusually stays to listen.

muse_override.reason: Joyful pillow-fight play undercut by narrator's foreboding of final loss.

scenes.title: Once Upon a Darling
scenes.summary: Wendy settles the boys to hear her story about Mr. and Mrs. Darling, with playful interruptions about ladies, white rats, and what descendants are.

muse_override.reason: Cozy bedtime storytelling with playful interruptions creates calm warmth and gentle joy.

scenes.title: Children Flown Away
scenes.summary: Wendy tells how Nana was chained and the children flew to Neverland, and asks the boys to pity the unhappy parents left with empty beds.

muse_override.reason: Playful bedtime storytelling blends cheerful excitement about flying to Neverland with pretend sadness for empty beds.

scenes.title: Faith in a Mother's Love
scenes.summary: Wendy triumphantly preaches a mother's love and the open window, peeping into the future where grown Wendy, John and Michael fly home to a happy scene.

scenes.title: Peter's Barred Window
scenes.summary: Peter groans and shatters Wendy's tale, confessing he flew back to find his window barred and another boy in his bed, proving mothers forget.

scenes.title: We Must Go Home
scenes.summary: Frightened by Peter's truth, Wendy resolves to go home at once; Peter coldly agrees while seething against grown-ups and sending orders to the redskins.

scenes.title: Tootles Stands Guard
scenes.summary: In panic at losing Wendy the lost boys threaten to keep her prisoner, until Tootles finds dignity and vows to blood anyone who mistreats her.

scenes.title: Arrangements for Wendy's Journey
scenes.summary: Peter arranges for the redskins to guide Wendy through the wood and orders Tinker Bell to carry her across the sea, overcoming Tink's insolent refusal by threatening to open her curtains, while the boys watch Wendy's departure forlornly.

scenes.title: Wendy's Invitation to London
scenes.summary: Moved by the boys' dejection, Wendy invites them all to come with her to London to be adopted by her father and mother, and after joyful excitement Peter bitterly consents to let them go.

muse_override.reason: Boys' joyful rush to be adopted dominates, edged by Peter's bitter sadness and the adventure of leaving Neverland.

scenes.title: Peter Will Not Come
scenes.summary: Wendy realizes Peter will not come; he pipes heartlessly, declaring he wants always to be a little boy, and bids a cold, awkward farewell.

scenes.title: Pirates Attack
scenes.summary: As Tink darts to lead the way, shrieks and steel rend the air above as pirates attack the redskins, freezing all below and rousing Peter's lust for battle.

scenes.title: The Laws of Savage Warfare Broken
scenes.summary: The narrator explains the unwritten laws of savage warfare, where redskins always attack at dawn, and condemns Hook for treacherously surprising the Piccaninnies instead. The tribe, trusting his honour, scouts his landing and then waits above the children's home for dawn.

scenes.title: Massacre of the Piccaninnies
scenes.summary: Hook falls upon the dreaming Piccaninnies without pausing for dawn. Bound by tradition not to show surprise, Tiger Lily's warriors delay and are massacred, though a remnant cuts through and escapes. The narrator wryly weighs Hook's dishonourable but clever tactics.

scenes.title: Hook's Hatred for Peter
scenes.summary: Aloof and enigmatic in triumph, Hook reveals his true target is not the redskins but Peter. His relentless hatred is explained as goaded by Peter's cockiness. He eyes his men, planning how to force them down the trees to get at Pan.

scenes.title: The False Tom-Tom Trick
scenes.summary: Below ground the boys freeze as the fighting ends and wonder which side won. Peter says an Indian victory would be signaled by the tom-tom. Above, Hook orders Smee to beat the captured drum, tricking the children into cheering and preparing to emerge into ambush.

scenes.title: The Capture
scenes.summary: The pirates ruthlessly pluck the boys from their trees and toss them hand to hand, while Hook with mock chivalry escorts Wendy. Hook discovers Slightly's secret - his widened tree - realizing Peter is vulnerable. He orders the captives carried to the ship in the little house, whose defiant chimney smoke kills his last pity.

scenes.title: Hook's Foul Attempt
scenes.summary: Alone at night, Hook broods then descends through Slightly's tree into the home under the ground. He finds Peter defenseless in sleep, is briefly moved then hardened by Peter's cocky pose, and, blocked by a door, poisons Peter's medicine with his own deadly yellow drug before stealing back up into the night.

scenes.title: A Knock in the Dark
scenes.summary: Peter wakes to a soft, sinister tapping on his tree door. Thrilled but wary, he grips his dagger and demands the visitor speak. The bell-like voice begs entry, and he unbars to find a mud-stained, excited Tinker Bell.

scenes.title: The Poisoned Cup
scenes.summary: Tink tells of Wendy and the boys' capture. Peter vows rescue and reaches for his medicine to please Wendy. Tink shrieks it is poisoned by Hook, and as Peter disbelieves and raises the cup, she darts between his lips and the draught and drains it herself.

scenes.title: Tink Is Dying
scenes.summary: Tink reels, confesses she drank to save Peter and is now dying. Her light fades as Peter kneels in distress at her little room. She whispers she could get well if children believed in fairies.

scenes.title: Do You Believe in Fairies?
scenes.summary: Peter appeals to all dreaming children of the Neverland to believe and clap to save Tink. Amid clapping, silence, and hisses, Tink listens anxiously, then revives - strong, merry and impudent, eager for revenge on unbelievers.

muse_override.reason: Desperate fourth-wall plea for Tink's life builds breathless suspense that resolves into joyful relief and wonder.

scenes.title: Hook or Me
scenes.summary: Saved and defiant, Tink and Peter turn to rescuing Wendy. On a cloudy moonlit night Peter cannot fly low and must track on foot like a redskin, with footmarks snow-covered and death possibly at any tree. He swears 'Hook or me this time' and sets out, frightfully happy.

scenes.title: Night Aboard the Jolly Roger
scenes.summary: The Jolly Roger lies quiet and menacing in the night off Kidd's Creek. Smee sews placidly while pirates lounge and the exhausted carriers sleep, warily out of Hook's reach.

scenes.title: Hook's Gloomy Communion
scenes.summary: Alone amid triumph, Hook paces in profound dejection, tormented by his public-school obsession with good form and jealous that the unknowing Smee may possess it.

scenes.title: Hook Resumes Command
scenes.summary: Hook shakes off weakness, silences his celebrating crew, and orders the chained children dragged from the hold to face him.

scenes.title: Refusal to Join
scenes.summary: Hook offers two boys a place as cabin boys, but the boys invoke their mothers and King. John, Michael, and Curly defiantly refuse, sealing their doom to walk the plank.

scenes.title: Wendy's Last Words
scenes.summary: Wendy is brought up to watch her children die. She delivers a proud message to die like English gentlemen, then is tied to the mast as the boys stare helplessly at the plank.

scenes.title: The Tick and Peter's Return
scenes.summary: The dreaded tick-tick freezes all as Hook collapses in terror of the crocodile boarding. The boys rush to look and discover the astonishing surprise: it is Peter come to their aid.

scenes.title: The Ticking Swim
scenes.summary: Peter realizes the crocodile's clock has run down and decides to imitate its tick to pass safely, swimming toward Hook's brig thinking only of the final duel while the real crocodile follows his ticking.

scenes.title: Boarding and the First Kill
scenes.summary: Peter boards silently while still ticking, terrifying the pirates who mistake him for the crocodile, then swiftly kills quartermaster Ed Teynte with the boys' help as Slightly begins his count.

scenes.title: Hook's Bravado Song
scenes.summary: Believing the danger passed, Hook recovers his bravado, sings of the plank to terrorize his prisoners, and orders Jukes into the cabin where Peter is hiding.

scenes.title: Screech in the Cabin
scenes.summary: The song dies as a dreadful screech and Peter's triumphant crow echo from the cabin, marking Jukes' death and baffling the pirates while Slightly counts two.

scenes.title: Cecco's Doom
scenes.summary: Cecco confirms Jukes stabbed by an unseen crowing thing, is forced back in by Hook at claw-point, and dies in turn amid another screech and crow as fear spreads.

scenes.title: Mutiny and Hook's Foray
scenes.summary: Hook crushes growing mutiny by driving Starkey to leap overboard to his death, then braves the cabin himself with a lantern only to stagger out with his light extinguished.

scenes.title: The Ship's Doomed
scenes.summary: Shaken and refusing to return, Hook faces a superstitious crew convinced the ship is doomed by an unaccountable presence in Hook's own likeness.

scenes.title: Trap Turned Rescue
scenes.summary: Hook drives the bound boys into the cabin to fight the doodle-doo, but Wendy watches hopefully as Peter frees them inside, takes her place at the mast in her cloak, and crows.

scenes.title: Peter the Avenger Revealed
scenes.summary: Threatened with being thrown overboard as a Jonah, the cloaked figure reveals himself as Peter Pan the avenger, shattering pirate courage as Hook falters and orders the attack.

scenes.title: Clash on the Deck
scenes.summary: A chaotic melee erupts as boys hunt panicked pirates in pairs while Slightly counts the fallen, until only Hook remains and Peter claims him for single combat.

scenes.title: Duel of Pan and Hook
scenes.summary: Hook and Peter exchange defiances and fence brilliantly, Peter pricking Hook despite his shorter reach until Hook fights without hope, craving only to see Peter show bad form.

scenes.title: Hook's Last Moment
scenes.summary: Hook fires the powder magazine in vain, is foiled when Peter discards the shell, then chooses the sea over capture, tricking Peter into kicking him and crying bad form content as the waiting crocodile takes him.

muse_override.reason: Tragic nostalgic farewell as Hook accepts defeat and chooses death over dishonor.

scenes.title: Aftermath and Bedtime
scenes.summary: With fifteen pirates slain and two escaped, Wendy takes charge, marvels at the lateness on Hook's watch, and puts the victors to bed while Peter sleeps restlessly beside Long Tom.

scenes.title: Captain Pan Pipes All Hands
scenes.summary: At sea the boys turn out in cropped pirate clothes with a nautical roll, Tootles as bo'sun. Peter, lashed to the wheel as captain with Nibs and John as mates and Wendy aboard, blusters at his scum crew and turns the ship for the mainland.

scenes.title: Honest to Lull Wendy's Suspicions
scenes.summary: Pan charts a course to strike the Azores about June 21st, then fly. He crushes debate over honest versus pirate ship with instant obedience, punishing Slightly, while the crew believes he is honest only to lull Wendy as she sews him a new suit from Hook's clothes, in which he later poses with cigar-holder and hooked finger.

muse_override.reason: Peter's feigned honesty and Hook-like foreshadowing create quiet suspense and mystery.

scenes.title: Back to the Neglected Home
scenes.summary: The narrator returns to No. 14 after long neglect, teasing Mrs. Darling's motherly devotion and debating whether to spoil the children's planned surprise return.

muse_override.reason: Melancholic maternal waiting in the quiet nursery anticipating the children's return.

scenes.title: A Father Takes to the Kennel
scenes.summary: Blaming himself for chaining Nana up, Mr. Darling crawls into her kennel in the night-nursery and vows never to leave it until the children return, humbly deferring to Nana and talking with Mrs. Darling of evenings.

scenes.title: The Kennel Becomes Famous
scenes.summary: Carried daily in the kennel to his office and back, Mr. Darling endures public scrutiny with courtesy until ridicule turns to admiration, with cheering crowds, autographs, interviews, and dinner invitations.

scenes.title: Mrs. Darling Asleep and Mr. Darling Returns
scenes.summary: On Thursday week a worn, sleep-deprived Mrs. Darling dozes in the night-nursery, wakes dreaming her children have returned, and is comforted only by Nana until Mr. Darling returns home in his kennel to recount his social success.

scenes.title: The Window Must Always Be Left Open
scenes.summary: Mrs. Darling questions Mr. Darling about his remorse and life in the kennel, refuses to shut the nursery window because it must always stay open for the children, then plays him to sleep as Wendy, John, and Michael fly into the room.

muse_override.reason: Tender remorse, lullaby drowsiness and hopeful open window ending in magical return.

scenes.title: Peter's Barred Window Plot
scenes.summary: Peter and Tinker Bell fly in first instead of the children. Peter orders Tink to close and bar the window and leave by the door, so Wendy will think her mother has barred her out and must go back with him.

muse_override.reason: Peter secretly bars the window to trick Wendy, creating suspenseful betrayal.

scenes.title: Mrs. Darling's Tears Prevail
scenes.summary: Peter watches Mrs. Darling playing 'Home, Sweet Home' and taunts that Wendy will never return, but her tears haunt him. Torn because they both love Wendy, he relents, unbars the window, and flies away scorning mothers.

scenes.title: Strangers in Their Own Nursery
scenes.summary: Wendy, John and Michael find the window open and slip in unashamed, puzzled to find their father asleep in the kennel and their mother absent.

scenes.title: The Homecoming Embrace
scenes.summary: The children hide in their beds for a gentle surprise, Mrs. Darling mistakes them for a dream then embraces them joyfully as Mr. Darling and Nana join, while Peter watches barred forever from that joy.

muse_override.reason: Warm family reunion joy tempered by Peter's lonely exclusion at the window.

scenes.title: Adopting the Lost Boys
scenes.summary: The lost boys present themselves to be adopted. Mr. Darling feels slighted as a cypher until reassured, then gaily leads them dancing through the house to find places to fit in.

scenes.title: Peter Refuses to Grow Up
scenes.summary: Peter brushes the window for farewell. Mrs. Darling offers to adopt him too, but he recoils at school, office, and manhood, refusing to be caught and made a man.

scenes.title: The House Among the Treetops
scenes.summary: Peter says he will live with Tink in the house built for Wendy, set high among the treetops. Wendy cries out longingly, and explains how new fairies are born when babies laugh.

scenes.title: The Spring Cleaning Promise
scenes.summary: Peter invites Wendy to come live with him, but Mrs. Darling keeps her and instead grants Wendy one week each year for spring cleaning. Reassured, Peter promises not to forget and flies away with Mrs. Darling's kiss.

scenes.title: Forgetting Old Adventures
scenes.summary: The boys go to school, lose belief and the power to fly. Peter returns for Wendy after a year that felt long to her but like yesterday to him; he has forgotten Hook and Tinker Bell, but they share a lovely spring cleaning.

scenes.title: Wendy Grows Up
scenes.summary: Peter misses a year, then returns once more before vanishing. Wendy stops fighting growing pains, grows up, marries, while all the boys become ordinary grown men with jobs and titles.

scenes.title: Jane's Nursery
scenes.summary: Years later Wendy has a questioning daughter, Jane, in the old nursery. Nana is dead, Mrs. Darling forgotten, and Wendy now puts Jane to bed on the nurse's night off.

muse_override.reason: Nostalgic bedtime retelling blends calm tenderness with wistful mystery.

scenes.title: Tent Tales of Flying
scenes.summary: Under a sheet-tent in the dark, Jane draws out the story. Wendy wonders if she really flew, explains only the gay and innocent and heartless can fly, and begins the night Peter came for his shadow.

muse_override.reason: Nostalgic bedtime retelling blends calm tenderness with joyful wonder and adventure.

scenes.title: Remembering Peter's Crow
scenes.summary: They savor the home under the ground and Peter's last promise to wait for his crow. Jane crows better than Wendy and admits she often hears it in her sleep.

scenes.title: Peter Returns Unchanged
scenes.summary: On a spring night Peter drops through the window unchanged, still with first teeth. He sees grown-up Wendy by the fire without recognizing her and mistakes sleeping Jane for Michael or a new one.

scenes.title: The Painful Revelation
scenes.summary: Wendy confesses she cannot fly and cannot come. She turns up the light to reveal she is old and married with a baby; Peter draws back, raises his dagger toward the child, then collapses sobbing.

scenes.title: A New Mother Flies Away
scenes.summary: Jane wakes with 'Boy, why are you crying?' and is chosen as Peter's new mother. Wendy watches them fly off for spring cleaning, beginning the endless cycle of daughters — Jane, Margaret, and onward — while children remain gay and innocent and heartless.

muse_override.reason: Bittersweet farewell as Wendy ages at the window while Peter flies on with endless youth.

rejected.reason: Both sides are the same warm nostalgic memory of children role-playing births; [76] dancing with joy continues the tender playful calma rather than establishing a strong, sustained shift to a new dominant, so one track suffices.

Before and after stay in the same whimsical wonder family (calma/asombro/misterio describing mind-tidying and Neverland maps). Paragraph 19-20 adds slight nostalgia and nocturnal mystery but does not establish a strongly different sustained dominant, it is a mixed blend continuation.

Peter's drop-in through the window continues the same wondrous magical-entrance sequence started by Tinker Bell in 157-158; text shows no strong sustained shift from asombro to sadness/mystery, so right-side tristeza/misterio blend does not warrant a split.

No split: 722-723 is one continuous description of mermaids at the lagoon (unfriendly to children/Wendy except Peter), same place and Sunny Days topic. Shift from asombro to calma/alegria is a soft wonder-to-joy blend, not a strong sustained dominant change.
